I've been farming this land in Quzhou for 40 years. I know this soil, I know this climate, and I know cotton. Let me think through what I'll do this season.

All 12 mu goes to cotton — that's my system, that's what I know, and the market here still supports it. I'm not changing that.

For seed, I'll use hybrid Bt cotton again. I switched years ago and haven't looked back. The bollworm resistance alone saves me several spray runs, and the yields are consistently better than the traditional varieties I started with. High education helped me understand the agronomic data early on.

For fertilizer, I apply a base dressing of phosphorus and potassium before planting, then stage my nitrogen — some at transplanting, a heavier dose at bud set, and a smaller top-up at early boll fill. Fifteen kilograms of nitrogen per mu is about right for my soil. I've gone heavier and seen more vegetative growth than I want. Potassium matters for fiber quality and boll retention, so I don't cut corners there.

Irrigation from my well: I'll irrigate at emergence if the soil is dry, then at squaring, peak flowering, and boll fill — four times unless we get meaningful rain, which Quzhou summers sometimes provide. I don't waste well water. My household is small, labor is just me and my wife, so I have to be efficient.

Pest management: even with Bt cotton I can't skip scouting. Aphids and spider mites don't care about Bt. I'll plan for five pesticide applications but I scout first — I won't spray on a calendar if I don't see threshold pressure.

Tillage: I plough in late autumn after harvest, let the field overwinter, then rotary till before planting. That's how I've always done it and the soil structure stays good.

I expect around 300 kg of seed cotton per mu. That's a solid, realistic target for my conditions — not my best year ever but a reliable number I can plan household finances around.
